name: Brownfield: collision-safe short-code generation
requirement: Make short-code generation collision-safe by retrying generation up to three times before failing.
whyThisType: The baseline already generated and persisted short codes and deliberately surfaced a unique-constraint collision as a conflict without retrying. The increment modifies that existing create path instead of adding an isolated subsystem.
baselineBehaviour: ShortUrlService.create generated one code, saved it, and let the short_urls unique constraint fail the request.
changedBehaviour: Up to three generate-and-insert attempts. A short-code duplicate is retried with a freshly generated code; anything else fails immediately. After three collisions the request fails with HTTP 409.
expectedOrchestrationBehaviour: Requirement is unambiguous, so the clarification gate does not trigger.
codebase-analysis identifies the existing create path as the change site.
PRE_IMPLEMENTATION approval is required before the existing behaviour is modified.
tests, security and documentation run in parallel, joined by validation.
FINAL approval is required before COMPLETED.
validationExpectations: One collision then a free code -> 201 Created.
Two collisions then a free code -> 201 Created.
Three collisions -> HTTP 409 after exactly three attempts, never a fourth.
An unrelated integrity violation (for example a not-null violation) is never retried.
A free code on the first attempt behaves exactly like the baseline.

tests: url-shortener-service: ShortUrlServiceCollisionRetryTest (deterministic generator + scripted writer, 5 tests)
url-shortener-service: ShortCodeCollisionsTest (only a duplicate short code may be retried, 5 tests)
url-shortener-service: ShortCodeCollisionRetryIntegrationTest (real PostgreSQL unique constraint, 4 tests)

intentionalBoundaries: The database unique constraint remains the final safety boundary; the retry only avoids failing a request a new code would fix.
The retry is bounded and never loops; the attempt budget is configuration, not a magic number in code.
Determinism in tests comes from stubbing the generator, never from waiting for a real random collision.
This business-level retry is unrelated to the orchestrator's agent retry policy (orchestrator.governance.max-task-attempts).
